item.title: How Rising Temperatures Likely Contributed to Nepal’s Deadly Flood
item.description: Climate change is causing glaciers to retreat and become less stable, upping the odds of catastrophic collapses.

item.description: The race to build a useful quantum computer is heating up

item.description: Fiio and Shanling release iPod doppelgängers with perks Apple's music players didn't have, perfect for the wired headphones revival.

item.title: Ukraine flags that Russia could have a secret fleet of autonomous military vessels stalking the seas
item.description: Ukraine warns Russia now fields increasingly advanced unmanned naval drones that can strike far offshore without detection for long periods.

item.title: Anthropic continues compute-gobbling streak in $45 billion deal with Nscale
item.description: The new deal with the infrastructure provider is the latest example of Anthropic's white-hot compute-gobbling streak.

item.title: Meta settles its alleged social media harm case for $18B and agrees to massive changes that may be almost impossible to enforce
item.description: Meta just settled the huge multi-state case against it, alleging that the social media giant's products harm teens. It's paying $18B, but are the promised product changes enough to transform the services and truly protect teens?

item.title: Democrats Just Might Win the Senate
item.description: Strategists in both parties have long thought that everything would need to go right for Democrats to take over Congress this fall. Their map, though, is becoming more forgiving.

item.title: The Meta Settlement Will Put Limits on Instagram for Teens. They’re Still Vulnerable
item.description: Child safety groups and former Meta employees welcome proposed changes to how the company’s platforms will work for teens. They also think states should have demanded more.
